nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, let $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ be inputs and let $t$ and $y$ be natural numbers. If, after $t$ steps of $P$ from the initial state on these inputs, the program counter is at least $\ell$ and the accumulator equals $y$, then the output of $P$ on these inputs is defined and equals $y$.
nodes.title: Output membership for RAM machines

nodes.summary: In a RAM state with register contents $r$, a store destination resolves to a register index: the direct destination $n$ resolves to $n$, and the indirect destination $n$ resolves to the contents $r(n)$ of register $n$.
nodes.title: Register written by a RAM store

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$ and $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ inputs. Run $P$ from the initial state on these inputs. If for some $t$ the program counter after $t$ steps is at least $\ell$, the output of $P$ on these inputs is the accumulator after the least such number of steps; otherwise the output is undefined.
nodes.title: Output of a RAM machine

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, $s$ a state and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If the program counter after $t_1$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is at least $\ell$, then the state after $t_2$ steps of $P$ from $s$ equals the state after $t_1$ steps.
nodes.title: RAM execution stays at its halted state

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a program of length $\ell$, $s$ a state and $t$ a natural number. If the program counter after $t$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is at least $\ell$, then the state after $t + 1$ steps of $P$ from $s$ equals the state after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: RAM execution is stable once halted

nodes.summary: For a program $P$, a natural number $t$ and a state $s$, the state after $t$ steps of $P$ from $s$ is obtained by applying one step of $P$ to $s$ exactly $t$ times.
nodes.title: Bounded execution of a RAM machine

nodes.summary: The initial state on inputs $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ has program counter $0$ and accumulator $0$; register $i$ holds $x_i$ for $i < k$, and every other register holds $0$.
nodes.title: Initial RAM state

nodes.summary: In a RAM state with register contents $r$, an operand resolves to a natural number: the immediate operand $n$ resolves to $n$ itself, the direct operand $n$ to the contents $r(n)$ of register $n$, and the indirect operand $n$ to $r(r(n))$.
nodes.title: Value of a RAM operand

nodes.summary: If the program counter of a state $s$ is at least the length of a program $P$, then one step of $P$ leaves $s$ unchanged.
nodes.title: A RAM step is sticky at halting states

nodes.summary: Let $P = (P_0, \dots, P_{\ell-1})$ be a program of length $\ell$ and $s$ a state with program counter $p$, accumulator $a$ and register contents $r$. If $p \ge \ell$, the step leaves $s$ unchanged. Otherwise it executes $P_p$, where $v$ denotes the value of the instruction's operand in $s$: a load sets the accumulator to $v$, an add sets it to $a + v$, a subtract sets it to $\max(a - v, 0)$, and a store writes $a$…
nodes.title: One step of a RAM machine

nodes.summary: An addressing mode of a random-access machine specifies an operand by a natural number $n$ in one of three ways: immediate (the operand is the value $n$ itself), direct (the operand is the contents of register $n$), or indirect (the operand is the contents of the register whose index is the contents of register $n$).
nodes.title: RAM addressing mode

nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is RAM decidable when there is a RAM program, a finite list of RAM instructions, such that for every natural number $n$ the program, started with $n$ in register $0$ and with the accumulator, the program counter and every other register at $0$, halts (its program counter reaches or passes the end of the program) with $1$ in the accumulator if $P(n)$ holds and with $0$ in the…
nodes.title: RAM-decidable predicate

nodes.summary: A store destination of a random-access machine names, by a natural number $n$, the register into which the accumulator is stored: either register $n$ itself (direct) or the register whose index is the contents of register $n$ (indirect).
nodes.title: RAM store destination

nodes.summary: An instruction of a random-access machine is one of the following: load an operand into the accumulator; store the accumulator into a store destination; add an operand to the accumulator; subtract an operand from the accumulator, truncating at $0$; jump to instruction $q$; jump to instruction $q$ if the accumulator is $0$; halt. Here an operand is given by a RAM addressing mode, a store destination is a RAM store…
nodes.title: RAM instruction

nodes.summary: A state of a random-access machine consists of a program counter in $\mathbb{N}$, an accumulator value in $\mathbb{N}$, and register contents, a function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ giving the contents of each register.
nodes.title: RAM state

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
